meta.cut_arm_note: the cut arms (L1/L2) run at W=500 and are read against W2, because at W=100 the fusion emits only 100 candidates and the cut is inert by construction (measured: Δ exactly 0.0000, W/L/T 0/0/3 identical at W=100).
meta.graph_lane: NOT included — it fires on multihop only and is a second lever
meta.hyde: OFF — deliberately, so every arm shares one query vector (pre-registration §4). The DELTA is unaffected; the ABSOLUTE numbers are not production numbers.
meta.prefetch_note: prefetch pinned at 2000 in EVERY arm (not the shipped 1000) so the 64d lane is not the cap (§I66) — the absolute numbers are therefore not the shipped config's; the delta is what is read.

reranker_swallow.why_it_matters: ClusterCrossEncoderReranker.rerank swallows every failure and returns the pool UNRANKED (§I55), which makes a top-k comparison on that query inert by construction. Named and excluded per arm, per pre-registration §6.5.

meta.what: §I66 — the pre-registered A/B on the product retrieval path: do the downstream widths (the fusion output W, the re-score cut L) improve the endpoint the product ships?

E7_cut_can_move.note: the pool must exceed the top-20 cut or the metric is inert by construction (§G1's defect); the width arms' pools must grow with W; and the cut arms must show the pool's PAGE set moving, since L changes composition, not size.

negative_control_E4.note: E4' (re-registration §8): the negative control must be bit-exact on every METRIC; any metric mismatch VOIDS the A/B. Diagnostics (n_pool/n_pages) are reported and do NOT void — Qdrant's server-side RRF fusion is non-deterministic (§I67) and can move the pool by a chunk on a minority of queries without moving any metric.

power.note: n is fixed (every answerable text query), so power is reported, not chosen. §D9/§2 convention: n = ceil((1.96·SD/δ)²).
